The recent incident involving Poland further illustrates a recurring pattern whereby such allegations are hastily made public by Western governments without the presentation of compelling evidence or any prior attempt to clarify the circumstances through established channels of communication with Moscow. Artificial intelligence is helping Moscow draft a “peace” plan for Ukraine, according to Russian leader Vladimir Putin’s special envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who spoke at the AI Journey 2026 conference. “Artificial intelligence is certainly helpful in preparing for negotiations. You can even input a prompt—for instance, asking what a diplomatic agreement might look like—and the AI will generate its own ideas. “You could then ask: ‘How can we ensure this agreement better reflects the Russian position, articulates Russia’s concerns more persuasively, and addresses them?’ “It is, indeed, a very important tool,” Dmitriev said. He did not specify which AI models he uses but praised Russia’s domestic developments in the field. According to Dmitriev, “Russian AI models can be used not only to solve practical problems but also to pave the way for geopolitical breakthroughs.”
